newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: French navy begins cooperation with S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: French navy begins cooperation with S.Africa.

text.p: The French navy command and supply ship Somme arrived off Simonstown naval base on Thursday to inaugurate a South African maintenance contract for France's Indian Ocean fleet.
The 17,900-tonne flagship of the Indian Ocean fleet will spend three weeks at Simonstown on the Cape peninsula undergoing dry dock maintenance.
Kevin Hanafey, executive of the state weapons agency Armscor which has the contract with the French navy, told reporters the work on the Somme would be worth about one million rand ($222,000).

"The longer-term agreement runs for 10 years but it's not a fixed agreement in that we will have dedicated ships coming in, it depends on the scheduling of the ships in the Indian Ocean, it depends on the availability of the docks, and the scope of the work," Hanafey said.

He said the contract with the French, signed under terms of a November 1994 defence agreement between Paris and Pretoria, marked the first major foreign naval involvement in Simonstown since Britain pulled out during the apartheid years under the strictures of the U.N. arms embargo.
The French Indian Ocean fleet comprises the Somme, two support ships and four frigates.
Asked if the fleet was monitoring events in Iraq, the commander of the Somme, Eric Abadie, said France had no warships in the Gulf at the moment.
